title: Why does China worry about one narrow strait?

post.caption: The World's Chokepoints: the Strait of Malacca. The Malacca Sultanate, the Portuguese (1511), the Dutch (1641), Raffles and Singapore (1819), the 1824 split, pirates and patrols, and China's 'Malacca dilemma'. Images: public domain (incl. NASA). Map data: Natural Earth.

beats.speaker: q
beats.text: Why does China worry about one narrow strait?

beats.speaker: a
beats.text: Because about a quarter of the world's traded goods pass through it: the Strait of Malacca.

beats.speaker: q
beats.text: Where exactly is it?

beats.speaker: a
beats.text: Between Malaysia and the Indonesian island of Sumatra. It runs about nine hundred kilometres, down to Singapore.

beats.speaker: a
beats.text: Near Singapore, the shipping channel is under three kilometres wide.

beats.speaker: q
beats.text: Who controlled it first?

beats.speaker: a
beats.text: Around 1400, a prince named Parameswara founded the port of Malacca. Chinese treasure fleets came to trade.

beats.speaker: a
beats.text: In 1511, the Portuguese took it with cannons. In 1641, the Dutch took it from them.

beats.speaker: q
beats.text: And the British?

beats.speaker: a
beats.text: In 1819, Stamford Raffles set up a British port at Singapore.

beats.speaker: a
beats.text: In 1824, Britain and the Netherlands split the strait between them.

beats.speaker: q
beats.text: So why does China worry?

beats.speaker: a
beats.text: Most of China's imported oil sails through here. In 2003, President Hu Jintao called it the Malacca dilemma.

beats.speaker: a
beats.text: Block the strait, and China's economy could choke.

beats.speaker: q
beats.text: Is there another way?

beats.speaker: a
beats.text: Ships can go around through the Sunda or Lombok straits in Indonesia, but it costs extra days.

beats.speaker: q
beats.text: And pirates?

beats.speaker: a
beats.text: In the early 2000s, pirates attacked ships here regularly. In 2004, Malaysia, Singapore and Indonesia began joint patrols, and attacks fell.

beats.speaker: a
beats.text: Next time: the Strait of Gibraltar. Like the video and follow History Sketches.

beats.speaker: q
beats.text: And tell us in the comments what you think!
